rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the statutory good causes. The landlord must serve the required Notice to Quit, and a Notice to Cease where applicable.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including single-family homes, apartments, mobile homes and mobile home park land, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or three units and two or fewer rental units; hotel, motel or guest house transient or seasonal guests (unless the occupant has no other residence and lives there continually); a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemption for transient/seasonal occupancy and for units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member

rules.penalty: If a landlord evicts for personal occupancy and fails to occupy the unit for 6 months, the landlord is liable for treble damages plus attorney fees. If the landlord evicts to retire, board up or demolish and then uses the property residentially within 5 years, the landlord is liable for treble damages and a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.6).
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for illegal-occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted so the landlord can correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance from the landlord equal to six times the monthly rent. If the landlord does not pay at least five days before removal, a municipal fund may pay, or unpaid amounts accrue 18% interest and become a lien on the property.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted under the illegal-occupancy ground of the Anti-Eviction Act.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to evictions for correcting an illegal occupancy

rules.penalty: 18% annual interest on unpaid balance; lien on property
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.
rules.conflict_note: Guide cites N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(g) or 2A:18-61.1(h) for this rule.

rules.title: Prohibition on self-help evictions and lockouts
rules.requirement: Landlords may not lock out tenants, change locks, shut off utilities or remove tenants without a court judgment. Only a court officer acting under a warrant for removal may physically evict a tenant.
rules.penalty: Damages, court costs and attorney fees; treble damages where possession cannot be restored (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-8); possible disorderly conduct charge
rules.quoted_span: Self-help evictions, or lockouts, made by the landlord are illegal in New Jersey.

rules.title: Anti-reprisal protection for tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict, substantially alter the lease, or refuse to renew in reprisal when a tenant does any of the following: enforces legal rights, makes a good-faith code complaint, or joins a tenant organization.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for damages in a civil action
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).

rules.title: Foreclosure Fairness Act tenant notices and protections
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Within 10 business days after a foreclosure sale, the new owner must notify tenants in English and Spanish that they are not required to move. Any cash-for-keys offer must be voluntary and accompanied by the required notice.
rules.key_value: Notice within 10 business days; 90-day notice to quit for owner-occupant buyer
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in foreclosed properties containing one or more residential rental units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to properties transferred through foreclosure

rules.quoted_span: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale, letting tenants know that ownership has changed hands and that the tenants are not required to move because of the foreclosure.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act (conversions)
rules.requirement: Eligible senior, disabled, or disabled-veteran tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years, subject to income limits. Converters must notify tenants of the right to apply.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants aged 62+, permanently disabled, or qualifying disabled veterans who lived in the building at least one year before the conversion recording date and meet income limits.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: only eligible senior/disabled tenants in buildings undergoing condo/co-op/fee simple conversion, subject to income limits and timely application

rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

rules.title: Truth in Renting statement distribution
rules.requirement: Landlords must give each tenant the DCA Truth in Renting Statement within 30 days of its posting. They must also give it to each new tenant at or before lease signing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants with a rental term of at least one month in buildings with more than two units, or more than three units if the landlord occupies one.
rules.exemptions: Buildings of two or fewer units; owner-occupied premises of three or fewer units; hotels, motels and guest houses serving transient or seasonal tenants.
rules.quoted_span: The Act calls for distribution of the statement by the landlord to all tenants with a rental term of at least one month living in residences with more than two dwelling units,  or more than three if the landlord occupies one of the units.

rules.title: Security deposit cap of 1.5 months' rent
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed 1.5 times one month's rent, and that cap includes any pet deposits and prepaid rent such as last month's rent. Any annual increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant opts in by written request.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant in an owner-occupied 2-3 family dwelling may opt in by written request

rules.penalty: Unlawful use of deposit monies: disorderly persons offense, fine of at least $200 and/or up to 30 days imprisonment (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Security deposit holding, interest and notice requirements
rules.requirement: Deposits must be held in trust in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey institution, with interest belonging to the tenant and paid annually. The landlord must give written notice of the bank and account details within 30 days of receipt.
rules.key_value: Notice within 30 days; tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent if noncompliant
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords who collect security deposits on residential rentals.
rules.exemptions: Seasonal rentals of 125 consecutive days or less; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.penalty: Tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% annual interest toward rent
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

rules.title: Security deposit return within 30 days
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, by personal delivery or registered or certified mail. The deadline is 5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, and 15 business days after a Safe Housing Act domestic-violence termination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies subject to the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant opts in.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld plus court costs and attorney fees. Willful withholding from a tenant receiving government assistance carries a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Law Against Discrimination including source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate based on a protected class, including source of lawful income. Protected classes include race, creed, sex, familial status, disability, gender identity and sexual orientation.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; single-sex residences; age-restricted housing as to familial status.
rules.penalty: Fines up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)); monetary damages
rules.quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.

rules.title: Rent increases may not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: There is no statewide numeric rent cap, but an increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent ordinance. It may take effect only after the old lease is terminated with a valid notice to quit and notice of increase.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units (Anti-Eviction Act exception).
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.conflict_note: Municipal rent control ordinances may impose stricter caps. Under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5, newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after construction is completed. HUD-subsidized and NJHMFA-financed units are not subject to municipal rent control.

rules.title: No rent increases to cover conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be raised to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. This applies to all tenants in the building.
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.exemptions: Increases to cover new services or amenities are allowed.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to buildings undergoing condo/co-op/fee simple conversion

rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no state law establishing or controlling rents; rent control exists only through municipal ordinances.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
